title: Derived adjunction of a ringed sequence projection
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ have inverse image on underlying sheaves the constant sequence, with ring map given by $A\to B_n$. The functors $Lp^*:D(A)\to D(\mathscr S(B))$ and $Rp_*:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(A)$ exist and form a canonical adjunction. Its Hom bijection is the derived fraction extension of the ordinary correspondence $h:P\to p_*N\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto b\pi_nh(x))_n$. For one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], $Lp^*P$ is represented by the strict complex $(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], naturally in derived $P$. Ordinary direct image is $p_*N=\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}N_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Tags 0941 (section-derived-limits before lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change) and 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); application to the ringed sequence projection.

proof.text: Use the stated equivalence between strict semilinear systems and module sheaves on $\mathcal T$. The index category $\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ is small, so $\mathcal T$ is small in the same module universe as $\mathcal C$. Module sheaves form an abelian category. Under the equivalence a kernel has levels $\ker(f_n)$; a cokernel is the vertical sheafification of the levelwise cokernels, because covers have fixed index. Consequently exactness and quasi-isomorphisms agree with componentwise exactness and quasi-isomorphisms of strict systems. We may compute in $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ on $\mathcal T$ and interpret the result in $\mathscr S(B)$.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, first paragraph; ringed-module interpretation

proof.text: For a strict system $N$, define $L(U)=\{(z_n)\in\prod_n N_n(U):t_n(z_{n+1})=z_n\}$, with componentwise addition and $A(U)$-action through $A(U)\to B_n(U)$. Compatibility of the structural maps makes this action preserve $L(U)$. Compatible families of local sections glue uniquely in each $N_n$; their transition equalities hold after gluing by uniqueness. Thus $L$ is an $A$-module sheaf and is the limit of the scalar restrictions. A map from a constant sheaf $F$ to the underlying tower is exactly a compatible family $F\to N_n$, hence a map $F\to L$. Since $p^{-1}$ is the constant sequence, this is the underlying direct-image adjunction. Its induced $A$-action is precisely the action just specified. Therefore $p_*N=L=\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}N_n$, naturally in $N$.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, opening description of constant inverse image and limit direct image

proof.text: The ordinary module adjunction gives $p^*M=B\otimes_{p^{-1}A}p^{-1}M$ and $p^*\dashv p_*$. Since $p^{-1}M$ is constant and all covers are vertical, its tensor sheaf at level $n$ is $M\otimes_A B_n$: the presheaf tensor and its sheafification are computed at that fixed index. The transition sends $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes\rho_n(b)$, where $\rho_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$. For $h:M\to p_*N$, its transpose has local pure-tensor formula $x\otimes b\mapsto b\pi_nh(x)$. This is balanced over $A$ and compatible with transitions because $\rho_n(b)\pi_nh(x)=t_n(b\pi_{n+1}h(x))$; it therefore sheafifies. Conversely a strict $B$-linear family $f_n:M\otimes_A B_n\to N_n$ yields $x\mapsto(f_n(x\otimes1))_n$ in the limit. These maps are inverse: one composite evaluates at $b=1$, and the other uses $f_n(x\otimes b)=b f_n(x\otimes1)$. Both formulas commute with precomposition in $M$ and postcomposition in $N$.

source.place: Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, tensor/restriction proof, specialized to the sequence site

proof.text: Apply existence of unbounded K-injective resolutions to the small ringed site $(\mathcal T,B)$. Every strict-system complex $N$ therefore has a quasi-isomorphism $j:N\to I$ with $I$ K-injective as a complex of modules on the sequence site. The additive functor $p_*$ induces an exact functor $K(B)\to D(A)$: applying an additive functor degreewise preserves shifts and the finite-biproduct formulas for mapping cones and homotopies. The total-right-derived theorem now supplies $Rp_*:D(B)\to D(A)$, computed by $p_*I$. Through step 1 this has domain $D(\mathscr S(B))$.

Apply the general ringed-topos derived-pullback theorem to $p$, with source ring $A$ and target ring $B$ on $\mathcal T$. It supplies the universal $Lp^*$, inverts quasi-isomorphisms between flat-term K-flat complexes after termwise pullback, and supplies its canonical comparison isomorphism on every such complex. A flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to P$ exists on $(\mathcal C,A)$. The theorem identifies $Lp^*P$ with $p^*Q$, whose levels by step 3 are $(Q\otimes_A B_n)_n$ with transition $1\otimes\rho_n$. One $Q$ supplies the entire strict complex. The theorem's naturality and compatibility with composition of comparisons give the asserted naturality in derived $P$, independently of the chosen resolution.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, statement and proof

proof.text: Use the ordinary adjunction from step 3 and its termwise homotopy adjunction. The flat-term K-flat class is left resolving: every complex has a resolution in this class and termwise $p^*$ followed by localization inverts its quasi-isomorphisms, as established in step 5. The source of $p_*$ has unbounded K-injective resolutions by step 4. Apply the resolving derived-adjunction normalization theorem to these universal left and right derived pairs. It gives $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ naturally in both derived variables. More explicitly, for $q:Q\to P$, $j:N\to I$ as above and any chain map $h:Q\to p_*I$, let $\widetilde h:p^*Q\to I$ be the ordinary transpose. Under $Rp_*N\simeq[p_*I]$, the class $[h][q]^{-1}$ transposes to $[j]^{-1}[\widetilde h]\epsilon_Q Lp^*([q])^{-1}$, where $\epsilon_Q:Lp^*[Q]\xrightarrow{\sim}[p^*Q]$ is the left comparison. At each level $\widetilde h_n(x\otimes b)=b\pi_nh(x)$ by step 3. The normalization theorem and bifunctoriality give the same formula after further quasi-isomorphism denominators, hence exactly the canonical derived fraction extension of the stated ordinary correspondence. This uses the localized Hom bijection, without assuming that a fixed $Q$ represents every derived morphism by a chain map.
